name: Randomized Hospital Room Designs: Golden Ratio, Feng Shui, Evidence-Based Design
description: Faithful replication (still images) of the online randomized controlled trial in Zijlstra, van der Zwaag, Kullak, Rogers, Walker, van Dellen, Mobach & Kelly (2024), "A randomized controlled trial of Golden Ratio, Feng Shui, and evidence based design in healthcare", PLOS ONE 19(6):e0303032. Participants who have stayed in hospital for at least one night answer background questions and are then randomly assigned to one of four versions of a single-bed inpatient room with ensuite bathroom: a digital twin of a real Dutch hospital room (control), or a redesign following the Golden Ratio, Feng Shui or Evidence-Based Design principles. They see two pictures of the room and two of the bathroom, imagine recovering from surgery there and answer the 6-item STAI (1–4); after seeing the pictures again they rate the Supportive Hospital Environment Design Scale (sense of control 5 items, social support 4, positive distraction 4; 1–5) and the pleasantness of the room's appearance (1–10). Answers are keyed by condition. In the paper (N = 558) the Evidence-Based Design room lowered anxiety, Feng Shui worked indirectly through pleasantness and social support, and the Golden Ratio had no effect. Stimuli: the 16 room and bathroom images cropped from Figs 2–5 of the paper (CC BY 4.0); question wording from S1 Questionnaire. The template will be removed if the authors object. Differences from the original study: (1) the 2-minute walk-through video, the 3D floor plan and the written description of each room are not available and are left out, so participants see only the four still images; (2) eligibility is asked with two simple questions and ineligible people are thanked and stop, instead of recruitment through the Dutch Patient Federation; (3) the condition is drawn with simple random assignment in the page, so group sizes are not forced to be equal; (4) the "Where were you born?" options are kept from the Dutch original.
author: Zijlstra, E., van der Zwaag, B., Kullak, S., Rogers, A., Walker, D., van Dellen, S., Mobach, M., & Kelly, L. H.

config.description: Faithful replication (still images) of the online randomized trial of Zijlstra et al. (2024), A randomized controlled trial of Golden Ratio, Feng Shui, and evidence based design in healthcare, PLOS ONE 19:e0303032. After eligibility and background questions, each participant is randomly assigned to one of four versions of a single-bed hospital room with ensuite bathroom (a digital twin of a real Dutch room = control, or a redesign by Golden Ratio, Feng Shui or Evidence-Based Design principles), sees two pictures of the room and two of the bathroom, imagines recovering from surgery there and answers the 6-item STAI (1-4); after seeing the pictures again, the Supportive Hospital Environment Design Scale (sense of control 5 items, social support 4, positive distraction 4; 1-5) and room pleasantness (1-10). Answers are keyed by condition.
config.spAnalysisRecommendation: Between-subjects randomized trial: exclude ineligible participants (hospitalised = no, or last_stay psychiatric/rehabilitation/childbirth). Score STAI-6 (sum after reversing the three positive items), the three SHEDS subscales (sums) and pleasantness per participant; compare each design condition (answer key golden_ratio, feng_shui, evidence_based) with control by linear regression or ANOVA with Cohen's d; test pleasantness, social support, sense of control and positive distraction as parallel mediators of condition -> anxiety.
